svg.title: MMT V3 Core — Protocol Security Floor Plan
svg.desc: A large chess-style top-down building map of the MMT V3 Sui Move protocol, showing rooms, corridors, assets, controls, cameras, alarms, guards, and audit routes.
svg.text: MMT V3 CORE · PROTOCOL SECURITY FLOOR PLAN
CHESS-STYLE AUDIT MAP · TOP-DOWN BUILDING LAYOUT · ROOMS, ROUTES, CAMERAS, ALARMS, AND STATE OBJECTS
The perimeter is the trust boundary: deployment metadata, package identity, owned capabilities, shared objects, and transaction entry points.
NORTH SERVICE ROAD · deployment / package metadata approach
SOUTH SERVICE ROAD · authorized transaction approach / audit exit
WEST ROAD · owned objects / capability route
B · THE BANK / SHARED OBJECT BUILDING
Rooms are grouped by source modules and state transitions. Corridors are conceptual transaction paths, not physical network topology.
pool.move · reserves · growth globals · current price / tick
Pool · total liquidity · protocol fees · flash fees
Checks and state transitions are encountered here: ownership → pool pairing → slippage → accounting → receipt consumption.
fee growth · price limit · amount deltas
emission rate · end time · reward growth · debt
E1 · EVIDENCE DESK — deployments / Move.lock / test results
E2 · ACCOUNTING LEDGER — owed fees / safe_withdraw / debt clearing
E3 · INCIDENT DESK — alarms / traces / caught or cleared
F · ROUTE PLANNING STRIP / SCENARIO TRACES
Routes model protocol call order and invariant checkpoints. A marker is a planned transaction step; an alarm is a failed guard or a suspected accounting mismatch.
flash receipt → pool ID → repayment → consume
negative / boundary / sparse tick → observation read
Dashed routes are scenario traces; they describe protocol call order, not real-world instructions.
MMT V3 CORE · visual audit artifact · source objects are grouped by room for planning clarity · no external image dependencies
